candidates.claim: /preset favorite list fans one command out to up to 50 parallel presets-api reads that carry no user id, so presets-api's per-IP and per-user limiters both skip them. candidates.title: presets-api never enforces the author ban on moderator approve/revert; the only guard is moderation-worker's non-atomic pre-check
candidates.claim: PATCH /moderation/:id/status and /revert write status='approved' with no lookup of the author in banned_users, and requireNotBanned checks only the caller on the presets/votes routers. A ban hides only approved presets, so a banned author's pending/flagged rows stay in the queue. The only guard is moderation-worker's separate isPresetAuthorBanned pre-read, which does not run atomically with the write, so a ban that lands between the check and the PATCH (or any client that skips the pre-check) publishes the preset. This is the server-side half of moderation-worker-01.
candidates.evidence: git grep -n -i banned apps/presets-api/src/handlers/moderation.ts -> no hits; requireNotBanned mounted only at presets.ts:131 and votes.ts:30; prepareStatusUpdate WHERE id/status/content_revision only (preset-service.ts:458-464); prepareRevert WHERE id/revision/status/previous_values (:481-486); ban hides `WHERE author_discord_id = ? AND status = 'approved'` (moderation-worker ban-service.ts:686-688); pre-checks at moderation-worker preset-moderation.ts:186, commands/preset.ts:284, preset-rejection.ts:268.

candidates.title: Owner can keep moderator reject/revert permanently STALE_REVIEW with uncapped tag/category/link edits
candidates.claim: The content_revision trigger also fires on tags, category_id, secondary_categories, example_link and author_name. An owner edit that changes only those charges no daily slot (the text_edit reservation sits inside if(textChanged)) and leaves an approved preset approved, so it is capped only by the 100/min per-user limiter. Moderator /status and /revert are bound to the reviewed revision, and the reject flow is a human confirm, modal and typed-reason loop. An author looping tag edits about once a second therefore makes every reject return 409 STALE_REVIEW and keeps an offensive approved preset public. Ban (a direct D1 hide that is not revision-bound) and moderator DELETE still work, which bounds the impact.
candidates.evidence: schema.sql:64-78 and migrations/0014:5-19 trigger on `tags, ... example_link, secondary_categories`; presets.ts:653-655 textChanged = name/description only; :665-700 reserveDailyEvent('text_edit') only inside if(textChanged); :533-536 approved + !flagged -> no status write, no notify; :798-805 owner UPDATE binds presetRow.content_revision (server's own read); preset-service.ts:461 status WHERE content_revision = ? (moderator-supplied); moderation-worker commands/preset.ts:235-244 confirm-then-modal reject flow.

candidates.title: Ban keyed on one identity leaves the author's other-identity presets public and approvable
candidates.claim: banUser hides only presets whose author_discord_id equals the single target id and fills xivauth_id only when the target is itself a UUID, and isPresetAuthorBanned joins on p.author_discord_id only. If a user owns presets under both their XIVAuth sub UUID and their Discord snowflake (submitted on the web before linking, then through the bot before the next web login runs refresh-author), a ban on the snowflake leaves the UUID-keyed presets approved in the gallery and their pending ones approvable, and NOT_BANNED then blocks the re-key that would merge them for good. Precondition not confirmed: how often a split identity exists in production. The workaround is to also ban the UUID, but the confirmation embed shows only the target id's presets.

candidates.title: .chara Nickname/TypeName projection can be ill-formed UTF-16 (lone or split surrogates)
candidates.claim: boundedLabel cuts nickname/producer at 256 UTF-16 units with String.slice, which can leave half of a surrogate pair. The library also accepts lone surrogates from a \ud800 escape or raw string input, so the projected label can be ill-formed. The only effect found is a U+FFFD where the name is displayed (web card, bot reply); no security impact found.
candidates.evidence: chara-library.ts:148 `return value.length > MAX_LABEL_UNITS ? value.slice(0, MAX_LABEL_UNITS) : value;` Probe scratchpad/probe/xck-probe.mjs: `nickname-split-pair` (255 x 'a' + U+1F600) -> nicklen=256 wellFormed=false; `lone-surrogate-escaped` '{"Race":1,"Nickname":"\ud800abc"}' -> OK wellFormed=false. Output in scratchpad/probe/xck-probe.out.txt.

It reads each value once, rebuilds a fresh DTO and enforces vocab enums, canonical hex, 256-unit labels, 8 unique slots, <=12 models, <=24 channels, <=64 issues and a 256 KiB bound (chara-inspection-protocol.ts:344-790).

Every terminal path terminates the worker exactly once. A superseded or late answer cannot publish, and the loader generation counter plus SWAP cancel-first stop an older file from replacing a newer one (service l.169-191,255,260,317; loader l.49-60,79-120; chara-file-card.ts:358-361).

Only fixed codes cross the worker boundary, with no exception text. Core caps input at 8 KiB via readChara maxBytes and projects issue paths to known segments only (worker l.81-92; chara-library.ts:142-160).

File-derived strings (nickname, producer, file name, item names, acquisition lines) render via textContent or element properties (chara-ui.ts:211-215). The only innerHTML in scope is static SVG (glamour-block.ts:588, item-links-menu.ts:343).

Resolve request carries only the protocol-rebuilt {slot,set?,base,variant} models and the glasses row, matching charaHintGlamour. Only the Glamour Reader resolves (glamour-tool.ts:90), so Swatch's LOCAL ONLY chip is accurate.

Community preset submission takes only the typed draft name, never the nickname or file name (glamour-block.ts:1781-1806). The export filename carries no character name (glamour-markdown.ts:69). The clipboard HTML flavour escapes every value (glamour-markdown.ts:112-136).

External item links use fixed https hosts and encodeURIComponent on names; Lodestone encodes before converting %20 to + so names cannot add parameters; window.open uses noopener,noreferrer (item-links.ts:71-122; item-links-menu.ts:130-131).
chara logs are fixed strings or counts. Telemetry is chara_parse {ok, producer-bucket} only (chara-file-loader.ts:92-129; telemetry-service.ts:177-184).

candidates.title: /glamour embed truncation math fails when the notes tail exceeds the budget; the failed edit is silent
candidates.claim: If tail.length > ~3996, body.lastIndexOf('\n', EMBED_BUDGET - tail.length - 4) gets a negative position and returns -1, so body.slice(0,-1) keeps almost the whole body. The description then exceeds 4096 and Discord rejects the edit. The success-path safeEditOriginalResponse return value is ignored (apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/glamour.ts:185), so the user stays on 'thinking' and the trace records ok. Precondition: the tail is built from upstream item names (no length cap in api-worker cleanName, xivapi.ts:96). Realistic game names keep it near 2.6k, so this needs abnormal upstream data.
candidates.evidence: glamour.ts:606-607: if (body.length + tail.length + 2 > EMBED_BUDGET) { body = `${body.slice(0, body.lastIndexOf('\n', EMBED_BUDGET - tail.length - 4))}\n…`; } -- node probe (12-line body, 4100-char tail) -> description length 4968 > 4096. handlers/commands/glamour.ts:185 `await safeEditOriginalResponse(...)` result unchecked.

candidates.title: plain() leaves masked links and mention/timestamp tokens in upstream item names unescaped in the public /glamour embed
candidates.claim: Item names, acquisition lines and glasses names from api-worker (XIVAPI plus bundled tables) go into the embed description through plain(), which escapes only * _ ~ ` | \. Masked links [x](https://..), <@id>/<#id>/<t:..> tokens and @everyone text render as markup. allowed_mentions parse [] stops pings, so the remaining risk is a phishing masked link. Precondition: XIVAPI (a third party) or the build-time acquisition table is poisoned; no file-controlled string reaches these sinks.
candidates.evidence: glamour.ts:384-386 `return text.replace(/([*_~`|\\])/g, '\\$1');` used at :412 (GPOSERS values), :581, :591, :598 (notes). bot-logic discord-markdown.ts escapeDiscordMarkdown also covers > # [ ] ( ) and defuseMentions, but neither is applied here.

candidates.title: ko/zh item-name tables built from an unpinned Teamcraft staging branch with no recorded commit or checksum
candidates.claim: The ko/zh tables that ship in the api-worker bundle are fetched from Teamcraft's moving `staging` branch with no commit pin, and the meta file records only the branch URL, so the shipped data cannot be reproduced or audited. The sibling script build-acquisition.ts does pin a SHA and records it; and the Item.csv ref silently falls back to the literal `master` if the GitHub API call fails (line 138).
candidates.evidence: build-item-names.mjs:62-67 `TEAMCRAFT_BASE = '.../ffxiv-teamcraft/staging/libs/data/src/lib/json'`; :246 `meta.sources[lang] = SOURCES[lang]`; item-names.meta.json lists the staging URL with no sha and `itemCsv: "local ffxiv-datamining clone"`. Compare build-acquisition.ts:104-115 (pinTeamcraft resolves a SHA) and :538 (`teamcraftCommit`). Output is data only: tag-stripped by cleanName (:182) and written with JSON.stringify, so the effect is provenance, not injection. Reachability needs a compromised upstream plus a maintainer running the script and committing the result unreviewed.
